claims.subject: eco-cheques PC 200
claims.quote: Employees who worked full-time during the complete reference period are entitled to eco-cheques worth 250 euro, paid in the month of June.

claims.subject: eco-cheques PC 200
claims.quote: Payment: in June, usually on the electronic card of the eco-cheque issuer (Edenred, Pluxee or Monizze), together with the June salary.

claims.subject: eco-cheques PC 200
claims.value: 1 June of previous year to 31 May of payment year
claims.quote: Reference period: from 1 June of the year before payment up to and including 31 May of the year of payment.

claims.subject: eco-cheques PC 200
claims.quote: Part-time employees are also entitled, on a scale that depends on their working time (the sector scale published by the unions lists lower amounts for smaller fractions, e.g. 150 euro for half-time and 100 euro for less than half-time).

claims.subject: PC 200 annual premium
claims.quote: In June PC 200 employees also receive the separate annual premium (jaarlijkse premie) that is indexed each year.

question: What is the PC 200 salary indexation on 1 January 2026?

answer:
PC 200 salaries are indexed by **2.21%** on 1 January 2026. This applies to effectively paid salaries, sectoral minimum salaries (barema's) and the guaranteed minimum monthly income, under the normal indexation rules [be_agoria_pc200_index_2026].

Company-level CAOs can differ. For example, Brouwerij Van Dessel's CAO applies the 2.21% on 1 February, to base salary only [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel].

My documents give the PC 200 indexation on 1 January 2026 as 2.21%. This is the annual sector indexation for office employees. The Maes emails and ticket confirm that the 9 PC 200 office staff correctly received 2.21% [eml_maes_recovery][tkt_2026_0021_maes][cfg_maes]. The documents do not include the official press release itself.

The 2.21% does not apply to other joint committees:
- PC 124 (construction) is indexed quarterly, and the 1 January 2026 step was 0.21859% [tkt_2026_0021_maes][eml_maes_recovery].
- PC 330 (healthcare) was indexed by 2% because the public-sector pivot index was exceeded [tkt_2026_0024_az][slk_2026_01_12_pc330].

The Slack message of 6 Jan claims that all sectors get 2.21% on the health index [slk_2026_01_06_pc124]. That claim is wrong. The official sources, the client config and the tickets win over an informal chat message, because the indexation mechanism differs per joint committee [cfg_maes][cfg_az].

The final PC 200 index is 2.21%, published on 22 December 2025. For Van Dessel, it does not apply on 1 January 2026.

For Brouwerij Van Dessel, the 2019 company CAO moves the index to 1 February 2026 [cao_vandessel_2019]. It applies only to the gross base salary. The 145 euro brouwerijpremie is excluded, and it is indexed separately by 2% on 1 July [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget]. January is paid without indexation. The exception is employees whose base salary would fall below the indexed sector minimum, who get the sector minimum from 1 January [cao_vandessel_2019].

The company CAO wins over the sector 1 January rule for this client, under PAY-IDX-01 v2 [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel]. Other PC 200 clients get 2.21% on 1 January.

The January Van Dessel payslips wrongly contained 2.21% on total pay, because the CAO flag was lost in the engine migration. They are being corrected in the February run [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel].

The internal note's 2.13% was only a forecast and is not applied [int_nl_nota_index_2025_12][tkt_2025_0870_vandessel].

The PC 200 indexation on 1 January 2026 is **2.21%**. It applies to actual salaries and minimum scales. It is the final figure, confirmed by Agoria, Acerta and Securex [slk_2025_12_22_final] and in the SD Worx communiqué [be_fr_pc200_index_2026].

The 2.13% was an October 2025 Pro-Pay forecast [slk_2025_10_15_preload]. It is superseded, so the forecast is not the correct figure.

- **Delta:** Its payslips showed 2.13% because a manual override was left in its config. The central update on 24 December does not overwrite overrides. The fix is to remove the override and pay the 0.08 percentage point difference retroactively. This is pending client approval [tkt_2026_0012_delta]. The draft reply says it would be paid in the February payroll [eml_delta_complaint].
- **Mertens:** It has no override and its payslips used 2.21%. Ticket closed [tkt_2026_0019_mertens][cfg_mertens].

The PC 200 indexation on 1 January 2026 is 2.21%. It applies to actual salaries and minimum scales. It is the final figure, published 22 December 2025 and confirmed by Agoria, Acerta and Securex [slk_2025_12_22_final] and in the SD Worx communiqué [be_fr_pc200_index_2026]. Mertens and Maes correctly applied it [tkt_2026_0019_mertens][tkt_2026_0021_maes].

Per-scope differences:
- Forecast vs final: The 2.13% was an October Pro-Pay forecast [slk_2025_10_15_preload][int_nl_nota_index_2025_12]. The final 2.21% wins. Delta's payslips showed 2.13% because of a manual override. The fix is to remove it and pay the 0.08 point difference retroactively, pending client approval [tkt_2026_0012_delta].
- Brouwerij Van Dessel: The sector rule says 1 January on effective salaries. The 2019 company CAO says 1 February on gross base salary only, excluding the 145 euro brouwerijpremie [cao_vandessel_2019]. The CAO wins for this client under PAY-IDX-01 v2 [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel]. The exception is employees below the indexed sector minimum, who get the minimum from 1 January. The January payslips wrongly applied 2.21% and are being corrected in February [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel].
- Other joint committees: Slack claims 2.21% applies to all sectors [slk_2026_01_06_pc124]. This is wrong. PC 124 is quarterly (0.21859%) and PC 330 was 2% [tkt_2026_0021_maes][tkt_2026_0024_az]. The official sources and client configs win over chat.

question: What indexation should Brouwerij Van Dessel apply in January and February 2026, and on which salary components?

answer:
**January 2026:** No indexation. The central PC 200 index of 2.21% on 1 January was applied wrongly because the company CAO flag was missing after the engine migration, so January must be recalculated without it [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel]. The exception is employees whose base salary would fall below the indexed sector minimum. For them the sector minimum applies from 1 January [eml_vandessel_budget].

**February 2026:** Apply 2.21% on 1 February, on the gross base salary only. The brouwerijpremie (145 euro/month) is excluded [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel][eml_vandessel_budget].

The brouwerijpremie is indexed separately by a fixed 2% on 1 July [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel]. The CAO flag was re-entered in the engine on 3 February 2026 [hnd_vandessel_2026_09].

**January 2026:** no indexation. The 2019 company CAO pays January without the new index [cao_vandessel_2019]. The one exception is an employee whose base salary would fall below the indexed sector minimum. For those employees the sector minimum applies from 1 January [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget].

**February 2026:** apply the final 2.21% from 1 February, on the gross monthly base salary only. The 145 euro brouwerijpremie is excluded. It stays at 145 euro and gets a fixed +2% on 1 July [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget].

**Conflicts:**
- The company CAO overrides the sector rule (1 January, effective wages) for Van Dessel only, under PAY-IDX-01 v2. The internal note itself says clients with a company CAO follow their own date [int_nl_nota_index_2025_12].
- The January payslips that applied 2.21% on the total salary were wrong. The CAO flag was lost in the engine migration. January must be recalculated, with the correction planned in the February run [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel].
- The 2.13% Pro-Pay forecast is not used. Only the final figure counts [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel].

January 2026: no indexation for Brouwerij Van Dessel. The 2019 company CAO pays January without the new index [cao_vandessel_2019]. Exception: if base salary would fall below the indexed sector minimum, the sector minimum applies from 1 January [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget].

February 2026: apply the final 2.21% from 1 February, on gross monthly base salary only. The 145 euro brouwerijpremie is excluded. It stays at 145 euro and gets a fixed +2% on 1 July [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget].

Where sources differ:
- Timing: the sector rule says 1 January; the Van Dessel CAO says 1 February. The company CAO wins for Van Dessel only (PAY-IDX-01 v2), and the internal note says clients with a company CAO follow their own date [int_nl_nota_index_2025_12]. Other PC 200 clients (e.g. Mertens, Delta) keep 1 January.
- Scope: the sector rule and team note index effective wages (whole pay); the Van Dessel CAO indexes base salary only. The CAO wins for Van Dessel; the sector rule stays valid for other clients.
- Slack says Van Dessel "got 2.21 like everyone" in January. That describes payslips wrongly calculated on total salary after the CAO flag was lost in the engine migration. January must be recalculated, with the correction planned in the February run [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel].

question: Which of our PC 200 clients have open tickets about the January 2026 indexation, and what figure should each get?

answer:
I can't tell you which PC 200 clients have open tickets. My documents in this scope contain no ticket or client list, so you'll need to check the ticketing system for that.

The figure itself is 2.21% on 1 January 2026 for PC 200 [int_index_calendar_2026]. Earlier forecasts of 2.13% [be_propay_forecast_pc200] and about 2.2% [int_outlook_2025_11] were only forecasts made before the final health index was known. The official final figure of 2.21% wins.

Exception: Brouwerij Van Dessel's company CAO moves the indexation to 1 February. That client CAO overrides the sector default, but I have no document in scope giving the figure for that client. Other PC 200 clients keep 1 January. Delta's manual override still applied 2.13%, so it needs correcting to 2.21%.

Don't copy the PC 200 figure to clients in other joint committees [int_index_calendar_2026].

The passages don't show any open tickets for PC 200 clients, so I can't list clients by ticket status.

- The only ticket that covers PC 200 is T-2026-0230 (Verhaeghe Logistics NV). It is CLOSED, not open. Its PC 200 office staff correctly received 2.21% [tkt_2026_0230_verhaeghe].
- The Bouwgroep Maes correction (T-2026-0021) concerns PC 124 construction workers. Its 9 PC 200 office employees already correctly received 2.21%. The passage doesn't say whether the ticket is open [eml_maes_recovery].

The figure for any PC 200 client is the final 2.21% as of 1 January 2026. Clients that applied a provisional figure should correct it to 2.21% [be_securex_pc200_index_2026]. The forecasts in the newsletter were not final [int_outlook_2025_11].

In my scope, only Brouwerij Van Dessel (PC 200) has an open ticket on the January 2026 indexation: T-2026-0015, owned by Jan Peeters [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel]. I found no open tickets for other PC 200 clients in these documents.

Figure for Van Dessel: 2.21%, applied from 1 February 2026 to the gross base salary only. The 145 euro brouwerijpremie is excluded and gets a fixed +2% on 1 July. January must be recalculated without indexation. The exception is employees whose base salary would fall below the indexed sector minimum, who get the sector minimum from 1 January [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget].

Conflicts:
- The company CAO overrides the sector 1 January date and the effective-salary base for Van Dessel only [cao_vandessel_2019].
- The 2.13% figure was a forecast. The final figure is 2.21%, and policy PAY-IDX-01 v2 applies only final figures [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel].
- The Slack remark "2.21 like everyone" describes the wrongly applied January payslips [slk_2026_01_09_vandessel].

Only one PC 200 client in scope has an open ticket: Softwarehuis Delta (T-2026-0012, open).

**Delta: 2.21%.** Its payslips showed 2.13% because a manual Pro-Pay forecast override (IDX_PC200_2026 = 2.13) was loaded in October 2025. The central update to 2.21% on 24 December did not overwrite it [tkt_2026_0012_delta][slk_2025_12_22_final]. The plan is to remove the override and pay the 0.08 percentage point difference retroactively, after client approval of the correction run. The reply to the client is still an unsent draft [eml_delta_complaint].

**Mertens Interieur: 2.21%.** Its ticket T-2026-0019 is closed. Mertens has no override and no deviating CAO, and its payslips already used 2.21% [tkt_2026_0019_mertens][cfg_mertens].

**Conflict:** 2.13% was only an October forecast. 2.21% is the final figure and wins [be_fr_pc200_index_2026][slk_2025_12_22_final].

Two PC 200 clients have open tickets on the January 2026 indexation: Softwarehuis Delta and Brouwerij Van Dessel. Each gets a different figure or timing.

**Softwarehuis Delta (T-2026-0012): 2.21% from 1 January 2026.** Its payslips showed 2.13% because a manual Pro-Pay forecast override was loaded in October and the central update on 24 December did not overwrite it. The plan is to remove the override and pay the 0.08 percentage point difference retroactively, once the client approves the correction run. The client reply is still an unsent draft [tkt_2026_0012_delta][slk_2025_12_22_final][eml_delta_complaint].

**Brouwerij Van Dessel (T-2026-0015): 2.21% from 1 February 2026, on gross base salary only.** The 145 euro brouwerijpremie is excluded and gets a fixed +2% on 1 July. January must be recalculated without indexation. The exception is employees whose base salary falls below the indexed sector minimum, who get the minimum from 1 January [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel][cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget].

**Mertens Interieur:** Ticket T-2026-0019 is closed, and its payslips already used 2.21% [tkt_2026_0019_mertens].

**Where sources disagree**
- 2.13% (Pro-Pay forecast) versus 2.21% (official final): 2.21% wins, because the forecast predates the final health index [be_fr_pc200_index_2026][int_index_calendar_2026].
- Slack says Van Dessel got "2.21 like everyone" in January, but the company CAO sets 1 February. The CAO wins for Van Dessel only [slk_2026_01_09_vandessel][cao_vandessel_2019].

question: The final index is not published yet at the January payroll cut-off. Can we apply the forecast?

answer:
No. Under the current policy PAY-IDX-01 v2 (valid from 3 November 2025), forecasts such as Pro-Pay or the Payroll Pulse outlook may not be applied, not even temporarily [pol_index_v2]. This replaces v1, which allowed forecasts [pol_index_v1].

What to do instead:
- The January payroll cut-off is 27 December. Only final, published sector figures may be loaded [pol_index_v2].
- If the final figure is still unavailable on 27 December, run January payroll without the indexation and apply it retroactively in the February payroll [pol_index_v2].
- Check the client config first. A client CAO that deviates from the sector rule (other date or base) always takes precedence [pol_index_v2]. For example, Van Dessel's CAO shifts the index to 1 February [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel].

No, don't apply the forecast. Policy v2 (valid from 3 Nov 2025) forbids loading any forecast, even temporarily. Only final, published sector figures may be loaded [pol_index_v2]. It replaces v1, which allowed forecasts and set a 20 December cut-off [pol_index_v1]. So v2 wins because it is newer.

What to do:
- The January cut-off is 27 December, not 20 December [pol_index_v2].
- If the final figure is still missing on 27 December, run January payroll without the indexation. Apply it retroactively in the February payroll [pol_index_v2].
- Check the client config first. A company CAO that deviates from the sector rule takes precedence for that client [pol_index_v2].

The centenindex note concerns the 1 July 2026 step (2.81%) in PC 111 and PC 209. It doesn't change this January rule [int_centenindex_note_2026].

No, don't load the forecast as final. The forecasts were explicitly provisional. Pro-Pay's 2.13% is a forecast that depended on the November and December health index figures [be_propay_forecast_pc200]. The internal SD Worx outlook of about 2.2% says "Do NOT load any of these figures as final" [int_outlook_2025_11]. That newsletter also tells consultants to warn clients that January payslips will use the final figure. It points to the indexation processing policy for when the final figure arrives after cut-off. I don't have that policy text, so check it for the exact procedure.

The final PC 200 figure is 2.21%, effective 1 January 2026 [int_index_calendar_2026]. It wins over both forecasts because it is based on the actual index. Check the client config for company CAOs that deviate. The conflict notes give Brouwerij Van Dessel, which indexes on 1 February, as an example. Don't copy the PC 200 figure to other joint committees. The calendar gives PC 124 at 0.21859%, PC 302 at 2.189%, PC 140.03 at 2.18% and PC 330 at 2% [int_index_calendar_2026].

question: What indexation should Van Dessel apply in January and February?

answer:
No, don't apply the forecast. Policy v2 (valid from 3 Nov 2025) forbids loading any forecast, even temporarily. Only final, published sector figures may be loaded [pol_index_v2].

What to do:
- The January cut-off is 27 December [pol_index_v2].
- If the final figure is still missing on 27 December, run January payroll without the indexation and apply it retroactively in the February payroll [pol_index_v2].
- Check the client config first. A company CAO that deviates from the sector rule takes precedence for that client [pol_index_v2]. Example: Brouwerij Van Dessel indexes on 1 February, while other PC 200 clients keep 1 January.

Where sources disagree:
- Policy v1 said to apply the latest forecast and used a 20 December cut-off [pol_index_v1]. Policy v2 forbids forecasts and sets 27 December. v2 wins because it is newer and replaces v1.
- For PC 200, the forecasts of 2.13% [be_propay_forecast_pc200] and about 2.2% [int_outlook_2025_11] were provisional. The final 2.21% from 1 January 2026 wins because it is based on the actual index [int_index_calendar_2026].

Don't copy the PC 200 figure to other joint committees. The calendar gives PC 124 at 0.21859%, PC 302 at 2.189%, PC 140.03 at 2.18% and PC 330 at 2% [int_index_calendar_2026].

question: Bouwgroep Maes has construction workers and office staff. What indexation applied to each in January 2026?

answer:
**January 2026:** no indexation. The company CAO pays January without the new index [cao_vandessel_2019]. The one exception is an employee whose base salary would fall below the indexed sector minimum. For that employee the sector minimum applies from 1 January [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget].

**February 2026:** apply the final 2.21% from 1 February, on the gross base salary only. Exclude the 145 euro brouwerijpremie. That premium gets a fixed +2% on 1 July [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget].

**Conflicts:**
- The sector date of 1 January and the Slack remark that Van Dessel "got 2.21 like everyone" are wrong for this client. The company CAO overrides the sector default under PAY-IDX-01 v2 [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel][slk_2026_01_09_vandessel].
- The January payslips already contain 2.21%. They were a migration error, because the CAO flag was lost. They must be recalculated without the index, with the correction planned in the February run [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel].
- The 2.13% forecast is not valid. Only the final 2.21% is applied [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel][int_nl_nota_index_2025_12].

**January 2026:** No indexation. The central 2.21% applied on 1 January was a mistake, because the company CAO flag was lost in the engine migration, and January must be recalculated without it [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel]. The exception is employees whose base salary would fall below the indexed sector minimum. For them the sector minimum applies from 1 January [eml_vandessel_budget].

**February 2026:** Apply 2.21% on 1 February to the gross base salary only. The brouwerijpremie (145 euro/month) is excluded [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel][eml_vandessel_budget]. The premium is indexed separately by a fixed 2% on 1 July [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel].

The 2.21% is the PC 200 figure [be_securex_pc200_index_2026]. The company CAO of 2019 only changes the date and the base [slk_2026_01_09_vandessel].

In January 2026, the two groups at Bouwgroep Maes received different indexations:

- **Construction workers (PC 124):** 0.21859% on 1 January 2026, applied to hourly wages and to the food and housing allowance [tkt_2026_0021_maes][eml_maes_recovery][cfg_maes].
- **Office staff (PC 200):** 2.21%, the annual indexation on 1 January [tkt_2026_0021_maes][cfg_maes].

The Slack message saying 2.21% applied to all sectors [slk_2026_01_06_pc124] is wrong. It led to the workers being overpaid, and the ticket and email correct it. The client config also says never to apply one population's indexation to the other [cfg_maes].

Bouwgroep Maes had two different January 2026 indexations:

- **Construction workers (58, PC 124):** quarterly indexation of 0.21859% on 1 January 2026. It applies to hourly wages and to the food and housing allowance [tkt_2026_0021_maes][cfg_maes]. The next step is 1 April 2026 [eml_maes_recovery].
- **Office staff (9, PC 200):** the annual indexation of 2.21% on 1 January [tkt_2026_0021_maes][eml_maes_recovery].

The workers wrongly received 2.21%. The correction is planned in the February payroll, with the recovery spread over three months, pending client confirmation [eml_maes_recovery].

Conflict: a Slack thread said 2.21% applied "across the board" to all sectors [slk_2026_01_06_pc124]. That is wrong. The ticket, the client config sheet and the email say the figure is PC 200-specific, and the config sheet says never to apply one population's indexation to the other. Those sources win over the Slack chat.

Bouwgroep Maes had two different indexations on 1 January 2026:

- Construction workers (58, PC 124): quarterly indexation of 0.21859%. It applies to hourly wages and to the food and housing allowance [tkt_2026_0021_maes][cfg_maes]. The next step is 1 April 2026 [eml_maes_recovery].
- Office staff (9, PC 200): annual indexation of 2.21% [tkt_2026_0021_maes][eml_maes_recovery].

Correction needed: the workers wrongly received 2.21%. The correction is planned in the February payroll, with recovery spread over three months, pending client confirmation [eml_maes_recovery].

Sources disagree:
- Slack side: a thread said 2.21% applied "across the board" to all sectors, on the health index [slk_2026_01_06_pc124].
- Official side: the ticket, the client config sheet, the email and the official press release say 2.21% is specific to PC 200. PC 124 is quarterly with its own percentage, and other joint committees (e.g. PC 330, which follows the public-sector pivot index) each have their own mechanism [tkt_2026_0021_maes][cfg_maes][eml_maes_recovery].
- Which wins: the official sources win over the Slack chat. The config sheet also says never to apply one population's indexation to the other.

question: Who should I ask about PC 200 year-end bonus rules, and did anything change for 2026?

answer:
Ask Jan Peeters. He has owned all PC 200 topics, including year-end bonus, since 1 September 2025. Koen Janssens moved to the Ghent implementation team, and the wiki says to route PC 200 questions to Jan, not Koen [onb_ownership_2025_update].

So yes, ownership changed. The 2024 onboarding page named Koen as the PC 200 expert [onb_ownership_2024], but the 2025 update replaced that.

The Slack message of 5 Jan 2026 still points to Koen [slk_2026_01_05_owner]. It conflicts with the wiki. The wiki update wins because it is the official onboarding policy, and the Slack remark looks like outdated knowledge.

My documents don't cover whether the year-end bonus rules themselves changed for 2026. They only cover who owns the topic. Jan Peeters is the person to ask about that.

Direct answer for Van Dessel:

January 2026: no indexation. The company CAO pays January without the new index [cao_vandessel_2019]. The only exception is an employee whose base salary would fall below the indexed sector minimum; the sector minimum applies to that employee from 1 January [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget].

February 2026: apply the final 2.21% from 1 February, on gross base salary only. Exclude the 145 euro brouwerijpremie, which gets a fixed +2% on 1 July [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget]. The 2.13% forecast is not valid [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel][int_nl_nota_index_2025_12].

Action: the January payslips already contain 2.21% because of a migration error that lost the CAO flag. Recalculate them without the index and plan the correction in the February run [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel].

Differences by scope (sources side by side):
- Timing: the sector rule says 1 January, while Van Dessel's 2019 company CAO says 1 February. The company CAO wins for Van Dessel only, because PAY-IDX-01 v2 lets a client CAO override the sector default [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel]. Other PC 200 clients (e.g. Mertens, Delta) keep 1 January.
- Base: the sector rule indexes effective salaries (whole pay), while the Van Dessel CAO indexes base salary only. The CAO wins for Van Dessel; the sector rule holds elsewhere.
- Slack says Van Dessel "got 2.21 like everyone" [slk_2026_01_09_vandessel]. That describes the wrongly processed January payslips and is less authoritative than the CAO.

question: What indexation do we get in 2026, and what did Softwarehuis Delta get? Do other clients also index on 1 February?

answer:
PC 200 indexation for 2026 is 2.21%, effective 1 January 2026. It applies to wages actually paid, sector minimum scales and the guaranteed average monthly minimum income. The figure is final. It is based on the smoothed health index for Nov–Dec 2025 against Nov–Dec 2024. The ~2.13% figure was an October forecast and is superseded, so 2.21% wins [be_fr_pc200_index_2026].

I can't answer the other two parts from my documents. They contain nothing on what Softwarehuis Delta received, nothing on the Delta or Mertens tickets, and nothing on whether other clients index on 1 February. I won't guess. The Delta/Mertens ticket and Slack sources are not in my corpus.

The 2026 PC 200 index is 2.21%, not the 2.13% forecast. The 2.13% was never preloaded, because only final figures are applied [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel].

Softwarehuis Delta: I have no document on it, so I can't say what it got.

Brouwerij Van Dessel: the company CAO moves the index to 1 February and applies it to the gross base salary only. The 145 euro brouwerijpremie is excluded and rises a fixed 2% on 1 July. January is paid without indexation, unless the base salary would fall below the indexed sector minimum, in which case the minimum applies from 1 January [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget]. The January payslips wrongly applied 2.21% on 1 January to the total pay, because the CAO flag was missing after the migration. They are being corrected in the February run [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel].

Other clients: my documents don't show any other client indexing on 1 February. This CAO applies to Van Dessel only. The other PC 200 clients follow the sector rule, which indexes effective salaries on 1 January.

The passages don't say which joint committee "we" belong to or which one Softwarehuis Delta falls under, and none mentions a 1 February indexation, so I can only give the January 2026 figures by committee:

- **PC 200 (employees):** +2.21% on 1 January 2026, applied to actual salaries, sector minimum scales and the guaranteed minimum monthly income [be_agoria_pc200_index_2026][be_sdworx_press_pc200_221][be_bbtk_indexeringen_jan2026]. If Softwarehuis Delta is a PC 200 client, which is plausible for a software company but not confirmed in the passages, this is the figure that would apply.
- **PC 330.01/.02/.04 (health care):** +2% in January 2026 [be_bbtk_indexeringen_jan2026].
- **PC 124 (construction):** +0.21859% on 1 January 2026, with further quarterly steps on 1 April, 1 July and 1 October [be_pc124_index_q1_2026].

**1 February:** none of the passages mentions a 1 February indexation for any committee. The January figures are specific to each committee and must not be copied across [be_sdworx_press_pc200_221][be_pc124_index_q1_2026].

To give a definite answer, I would need your own joint committee and Softwarehuis Delta's committee.

PC 200 indexation for 2026 is 2.21%, effective 1 January 2026. It applies to wages actually paid, sector minimum scales and the guaranteed average monthly minimum income. The figure is final [be_fr_pc200_index_2026].

Where sources disagree: the ~2.13% was an October forecast and was never preloaded, since only final figures are applied [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel]. 2.21% wins because it is the final figure.

Softwarehuis Delta: none of the sources cover it, so I can't say what it received. The Delta and Mertens tickets were not available to the specialists. Please check the Delta ticket directly.

Other clients indexing on 1 February: the only one found is Brouwerij Van Dessel. Its company CAO moves the index to 1 February and applies it to gross base salary only. The 145 euro brouwerijpremie is excluded and rises a fixed 2% on 1 July. January is unindexed, unless base pay would fall below the indexed sector minimum, in which case the minimum applies from 1 January [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget].

Per-scope difference: the sector rule indexes effective salaries (whole pay) on 1 January. The Van Dessel CAO is more specific and applies to Van Dessel only. Other PC 200 clients follow the sector rule. The sources show no other client on 1 February, but that isn't proof none exist.

Van Dessel's January payslips wrongly applied 2.21% to total pay because the CAO flag was lost after migration. They are being corrected in the February run [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel].

question: Did all our clients move to the 8.91 euro employer share for meal vouchers on 1 January 2026?

answer:
**No.** The 8.91 euro employer share is a maximum, not an automatic increase. Under policy PAY-MV-02 v2, a client can only raise it if a sector CAO, a company CAO or (without union delegation) individual written agreements provide for it. The consultant must have the signed document in the client file before changing the config. Clients that do nothing keep their existing voucher value [pol_mealvoucher_v2][int_mealvoucher_news_2025_12].

The Slack message saying the engine sets 8.91 for all clients automatically [slk_2026_01_02_mealvouchers] contradicts the policy and the newsletter, so don't rely on it.

The Van Dessel ticket confirms this. The client is still at an employer share of 6.91 euro (8 euro voucher) and is waiting on a signed CAO before any change [tkt_2026_0102_vandessel].

No. The 8.91 euro employer share is a maximum that became possible from 1 January 2026. It is not automatic. A client can only move to it with a sector or company CAO, or, without a union delegation, individual written agreements. The signed document must be in the client file before the config is changed. Clients that do nothing keep their existing voucher value [pol_mealvoucher_v2][int_mealvoucher_news_2025_12][be_mealvouchers_2026].

The Slack claim that the engine sets 8.91 for all clients is wrong. Policy v2 is the official internal policy and the newsletter and Liantis/Acerta agree with it, so it wins [slk_2026_01_02_mealvouchers].

Van Dessel is a concrete counterexample. Its config is still 8 euro with a 6.91 employer share, pending a signed CAO [tkt_2026_0102_vandessel]. The ticket dates from 3 Feb 2026, so a person should confirm the current engine config.

No, not all clients moved to 8.91 euro on 1 January 2026. 8.91 is a maximum employer share that became possible from that date, and it is not automatic. A client can only adopt it through a sector or company CAO or, where there is no union delegation, individual written agreements. The signed document must be in the client file before the config is changed. Clients that do nothing keep their existing voucher value [pol_mealvoucher_v2][int_mealvoucher_news_2025_12][be_mealvouchers_2026].

Per-scope difference:
- Van Dessel: the ticket shows an 8 euro voucher with a 6.91 euro employer share, pending a signed CAO [tkt_2026_0102_vandessel]. The ticket is dated 3 Feb 2026, so confirm the current engine config.

Where sources disagree:
- Slack says the engine sets 8.91 for all clients, including Van Dessel. Policy v2, the newsletter and Liantis/Acerta say it needs a CAO or written agreements. Policy v2 wins because it is the official internal policy and the external sources agree with it [slk_2026_01_02_mealvouchers].
- For Van Dessel, the ticket wins over Slack because it is client-specific and shows the actual config.
- Policy v1 (8 euro face value, 6.91 euro share, from 2024-01-15) is superseded by the 2026 maxima (10 euro and 8.91 euro), which have the newer valid_from date.

Check each client's file for a signed CAO or agreements rather than assuming 8.91.

question: What is the maximum telework allowance we can pay per month in September 2026?

answer:
The maximum is **164.21 euro per month** from 1 September 2026, up from 160.99 euro [be_telework_2026]. The helpdesk ticket gives the same figure [tkt_2026_0311_delta].

The policy page still shows 160.99 euro (valid from 1 March 2026, next review September 2026) [pol_telework_v2]. It is outdated for September.

If a client's config uses the "maximum" flag, it follows the central parameter. The ticket says that parameter must be updated first before September payslips use 164.21 [tkt_2026_0311_delta]. Clients with a fixed amount are not changed automatically [pol_telework_v2].

The maximum telework (flat-rate office) allowance for September 2026 is **164.21 EUR per month**, exempt from social security contributions. It applies from 1 September 2026 [be_telework_2026]. The Slack announcement confirms it, and the central parameter was updated that night [slk_2026_09_01_telework].

Older figures don't apply:
- 157.83 EUR applied from March 2025 [be_telework_2025][pol_telework_v1].
- 160.99 EUR applied from 1 March to 31 August 2026 [pol_telework_v2].

Policy PAY-TW-03 v2 still says 160.99 EUR. The wiki is outdated, and an update is planned [slk_2026_09_01_telework]. The newest valid_from from the official source wins.

Conditions: structural, regular telework equal to one working day per week, assessed monthly. Clients may pay less than the maximum [pol_telework_v1]. Clients on a fixed lower amount aren't changed automatically [pol_telework_v2]. Delta follows the central maximum, so it gets 164.21 EUR [tkt_2026_0140_delta][tkt_2026_0311_delta].

The maximum telework allowance you can pay for September 2026 is 164.21 EUR per month, exempt from social security contributions. It applies from 1 September 2026 [be_telework_2026]. A Slack announcement confirms it, and the central parameter was updated [slk_2026_09_01_telework].

Sources disagree on the amount:
- Policy PAY-TW-03 v2 still says 160.99 EUR [pol_telework_v2]. That figure applied only from 1 March to 31 August 2026. The official Securex/Salary Solution source gives 164.21 EUR from 1 September 2026, and its valid_from is newer, so 164.21 EUR wins. The wiki is outdated and an update is planned [slk_2026_09_01_telework].
- 157.83 EUR was the amount from March 2025 [be_telework_2025][pol_telework_v1]. It is superseded.

Per-scope differences:
- Delta: its config was a fixed 157.83 EUR, but it was changed on 2026-04-04 to follow the central maximum. Delta therefore gets 164.21 EUR [tkt_2026_0140_delta][tkt_2026_0311_delta].
- Clients on a fixed lower amount are not changed automatically [pol_telework_v2]. Clients may also pay less than the maximum [pol_telework_v1].

Conditions: the telework must be structural and regular, equal to one working day per week, and is assessed monthly [pol_telework_v1].

question: Which reference period do we use for the June 2026 PC 200 eco-cheques, and which clients are skipped?

answer:
**Reference period:** 1 June 2025 through 31 May 2026 (June of the prior year to May of the payment year) [be_pc200_ecocheques]. The policy PAY-ECO-04 confirms the same rule [pol_ecocheque_v1]. The Slack message naming calendar year 2025 conflicts with both and is not supported by the sector info or the policy, so the pro-rata run on calendar 2025 should be redone [slk_2026_05_28_ecocheques].

**Clients skipped:** The passages don't name any clients that are skipped. The only related point is that companies may convert eco-cheques into an equivalent benefit through a company CAO [be_pc200_ecocheques]. Whether any client has done so is not stated. The centenindex note concerns PC 111/209 metal indexation and doesn't affect eco-cheques [int_centenindex_note_2026].

My documents don't answer this. They cover January 2026 index forecasts and the 2026 index calendar, and they say nothing about eco-cheques. They give no reference period for the June 2026 PC 200 eco-cheques and don't say which clients are skipped. I won't guess. Please ask the PC 200 owner, or check the eco-cheque policy document, which isn't in my scope. For PC 200, the documents only say indexation happens on 1 January, at a final 2.21% [int_index_calendar_2026]. They also say that Brouwerij Van Dessel's company CAO moves its indexation to 1 February. That concerns indexation, not eco-cheques.

My documents don't answer this. The question is about the reference period for the June 2026 PC 200 eco-cheques and which clients are skipped. My scope covers only Van Dessel's company CAO on indexation, the preload request, the 1 January vs 1 February timing, and the CFO's February index question. None of these documents mentions eco-cheques, a reference period or client exclusions, so I can't give a reference period or a skip list.

What the documents do say is about indexation, not eco-cheques. For Brouwerij Van Dessel only, the 2019 company CAO applies the 2.21% index on 1 February 2026, to base salary only and excluding the 145 euro brouwerijpremie [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget]. Other PC 200 clients keep the sector date of 1 January. The company CAO wins for Van Dessel because PAY-IDX-01 v2 lets a client CAO override the sector default [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel]. Please check an eco-cheque source for the eco-cheque question.

My documents don't state the reference period for the June 2026 PC 200 eco-cheques, so I can't give it. The Delta tickets, the Mertens ticket and the Slack threads cover only the January indexation.

Skipped client: Mertens Interieur (BE-38802). Its eco-cheques were converted into a cafeteria-plan budget of equivalent value by a 2024 company CAO, so the eco-cheque run is skipped [cfg_mertens]. My documents name no other skipped client. Delta has no eco-cheque deviation in the documents I have.

Separately, on the index: 2.21% is the final PC 200 figure and wins. The 2.13% was an October forecast that stayed in Delta's config as a manual override [tkt_2026_0012_delta][slk_2025_12_22_final][be_fr_pc200_index_2026].

The documents don't state the reference period for the June 2026 PC 200 eco-cheques. No specialist had a source covering it (A20 and A12 found nothing on eco-cheques, and A21 said the same for its documents). I won't guess one. Please check the eco-cheque policy document or ask the PC 200 owner.

Skipped clients: only one is documented. Mertens Interieur (BE-38802) is skipped because a 2024 company CAO converted its eco-cheques into an equivalent cafeteria-plan budget [cfg_mertens]. Only A21 reported this, and the others didn't contradict it. No other skipped client is named. Delta has no documented eco-cheque deviation.

Related indexation points (not eco-cheque rules):
- Index: the final 2.21% wins over the 2.13% October forecast, which remained in Delta's config as a manual override [tkt_2026_0012_delta][slk_2025_12_22_final][be_fr_pc200_index_2026].
- Timing: the sector date is 1 January, but Brouwerij Van Dessel's 2019 company CAO moves it to 1 February, on base salary only and excluding the 145 euro brouwerijpremie. The client CAO wins for Van Dessel only, under PAY-IDX-01 v2 [cao_vandessel_2019][tkt_2025_0870_vandessel].

question: From when does the 21 euro per hour flexi-wage cap in horeca apply, and what does it mean for De Gouden Lepel?

answer:
The cap applies from **1 July 2026**, per the current policy and the helpdesk ticket [pol_flexi_v1][tkt_2026_0201_goudenlepel]. The December 2025 email from the account manager gave 1 January 2026, but the later policy and ticket supersede it [eml_goudenlepel_flexi].

**For De Gouden Lepel (PC 302):** the 22.50 euro/hour rate for the weekend sommelier is above the 21 euro cap, so payroll blocks it from the July 2026 payroll on. The client can either pay 21 euro/hour as a flexi-job or employ the sommelier on a regular part-time contract. The ticket is still open, awaiting the client's choice [tkt_2026_0201_goudenlepel][pol_flexi_v1].

The 21 euro/hour flexi-wage cap in horeca (PC 302) applies from 1 July 2026, subject to indexation [be_flexijobs_2026][pol_flexi_v1]. Payroll must block higher rates from the July 2026 payroll on [pol_flexi_v1].

Conflict: the Dec 2025 email says 1 January 2026 [eml_goudenlepel_flexi]. The official summary, policy, Slack and ticket all say 1 July 2026, and the ticket shows the cap was enforced from July. The July date wins, and the email's January date is wrong.

For De Gouden Lepel: the weekend sommelier's 22.50 euro/hour is above the cap, so the system refuses it [tkt_2026_0201_goudenlepel][slk_2026_06_30_flexi]. The options are to pay 21 euro/hour as a flexi-job or to use a regular part-time contract. The ticket is open, waiting for the client's choice. The 28% employer contribution is unchanged [pol_flexi_v1].

The 21 euro/hour flexi-wage cap in horeca (PC 302) applies from 1 July 2026, subject to indexation [be_flexijobs_2026][pol_flexi_v1]. Payroll must block higher rates from the July 2026 payroll on [pol_flexi_v1].

Where sources disagree:
- The Dec 2025 email says the cap applies from 1 January 2026 [eml_goudenlepel_flexi].
- The official summary, the policy, Slack and the ticket all say 1 July 2026 [be_flexijobs_2026][pol_flexi_v1][slk_2026_06_30_flexi][tkt_2026_0201_goudenlepel].
- The July date wins. It comes from the policy and the official source, and the ticket shows the cap was enforced only from July. The email's January date is wrong or premature.

What it means for De Gouden Lepel:
- The weekend sommelier's rate of 22.50 euro/hour is above the cap, so the system refuses it [tkt_2026_0201_goudenlepel][slk_2026_06_30_flexi].
- The options are to pay 21 euro/hour as a flexi-job or to move the sommelier to a regular part-time contract.
- The ticket is open, waiting for the client's choice.
- The 28% employer contribution is unchanged [pol_flexi_v1].

Since the client was told January in the email, it is worth clarifying the correct date with them when you ask for their decision.

question: Give Verhaeghe Logistics an overview of 2026 indexation and minimum wages per entity. Should their Dutch expats get 27% under the 30% ruling?

answer:
I can't give actual 2026 figures or confirm the 27% question, because my documents don't contain them. They give only the rules per entity.

**Rules per entity** [int_crossborder_policy]
- **Belgian entities:** Sector rules apply, including joint committee (PC) indexations. The PC owners are named in [onb_ownership_2024]. Verhaeghe's own PC and CAO settings aren't in my documents.
- **Dutch entity:** The statutory minimum wage is indexed on 1 January and 1 July. Holiday allowance is at least 8%. The 30% ruling applies to eligible expats. Belgian sector rules never apply.
- **Luxembourg entity:** Automatic index tranches of 2.5% apply from the month the tranche is triggered. The social minimum wage (SSM) applies.

**30% ruling:** The policy only says the ruling applies to eligible expats. It doesn't mention 27%. Don't confirm 27% from these sources. Ask the NL cross-border desk (Emma de Vries) to confirm the rate and eligibility [onb_ownership_2024].

Indexation and minimum wage figures also need to come from the desks.

**No, the Dutch expats should stay at 30% in 2026.** The reduction to 27% only applies from 1 January 2027 [nl_30pct_ruling_2026][eml_verhaeghe_nl_30pct]. The 2026 salary norm is 48,013 euro, or 36,497 euro for under-30s with a qualifying master's [nl_30pct_ruling_2026]. Employees who already received the allowance in December 2023 keep 30% for the rest of their ruling period. According to the draft reply, this covers two of the three planners [eml_verhaeghe_nl_30pct][nl_30pct_ruling_2026].

**2026 indexation and minimum wages per entity** [eml_verhaeghe_lu_frontaliers]:
- **Belgium, PC 140.03 (drivers and warehouse):** 2.18% on 1 January 2026.
- **Belgium, PC 200 (office):** 2.21% on 1 January 2026.
- **Luxembourg:** 2.5% on 1 June 2026.
- **Netherlands:** no automatic indexation. The statutory minimum wage is 14.71 euro/hour from 1 January and 14.99 euro/hour from 1 July 2026.

**2026 overview per entity (Verhaeghe Logistics)**
- Belgium, PC 140.03 drivers: 2.18% on 1 Jan 2026 [tkt_2026_0230_verhaeghe][be_sdworx_press_food_horeca_transport].
- Belgium, PC 200 office: 2.21% on 1 Jan [tkt_2026_0230_verhaeghe][eml_verhaeghe_lu_frontaliers].
- Luxembourg: 2.5% on 1 June 2026 [eml_verhaeghe_lu_frontaliers].
- Netherlands: no automatic indexation. The statutory minimum wage is 14.71 euro/hour from 1 Jan and 14.99 from 1 July. The later rate supersedes the earlier one from 1 July [eml_verhaeghe_lu_frontaliers].

PC 302 (horeca) doesn't apply to this client. For reference, the final figure is 2.189%, which replaces the ~2.1% estimate [tkt_2026_0027_goudenlepel][int_horeca_outlook_2025_11].

**30% ruling:** No. The cut to 27% applies only from 1 Jan 2027. In 2026 the maximum stays 30%, if the salary norm is met. Two of the three expats keep 30% under the transitional rule. This comes from Emma de Vries's draft reply, which hasn't been sent [eml_verhaeghe_nl_30pct].

**Direct answer on the 30% ruling:** No, not for 2026. The cut to 27% applies only from 1 Jan 2027. In 2026 the maximum stays 30% if the salary norm is met, and two of the three expats keep 30% under the transitional rule [eml_verhaeghe_nl_30pct]. This comes from Emma de Vries's draft reply, which hasn't been sent. Get her confirmation before advising the client. The general policy only says the ruling applies to eligible expats and doesn't mention 27% [int_crossborder_policy].

**2026 indexation and minimum wages per entity**
- Belgium, PC 140.03 (drivers): 2.18% on 1 Jan [tkt_2026_0230_verhaeghe][be_sdworx_press_food_horeca_transport].
- Belgium, PC 200 (office): 2.21% on 1 Jan [tkt_2026_0230_verhaeghe][eml_verhaeghe_lu_frontaliers].
- Luxembourg: 2.5% index tranche on 1 June 2026 [eml_verhaeghe_lu_frontaliers][int_crossborder_policy].
- Netherlands: no automatic indexation. The statutory minimum wage is 14.71 euro/hour from 1 Jan to 30 Jun, and 14.99 from 1 Jul [eml_verhaeghe_lu_frontaliers]. Holiday allowance is at least 8% [int_crossborder_policy].

**Where sources differ**
- Agent A25 gave no figures because its documents hold only the rules. Agent A10's documents contain the figures, so I use them.
- The Dutch minimum wage has two rates in the same email. 14.99 wins from 1 July because it has the later valid_from, so it applies now. 14.71 held until 30 June.

PC 302 (horeca) doesn't apply to this client.

question: I just inherited Brouwerij Van Dessel. Els asks urgently: how many of the 12 temporary unemployment days of March count for the December 2026 year-end bonus?

answer:
Only the first 5 days count as worked days (gelijkgesteld) for the December 2026 year-end bonus. The other 7 days reduce the bonus pro rata [hnd_vandessel_2026_09]. This follows policy PAY-EOY-05 v2 for PC 200, and the Mertens ticket draft cites the same 5-day rule [tkt_2026_0305_mertens].

Do not follow the Teams chat advice to set equated days to 12. It claims all temporary unemployment days count, but it conflicts with the handover note and the policy [teams_2026_09_24_vandessel]. The union's claim that all 12 count is not supported either [tkt_2026_0321_vandessel]. If you want to be sure, Jan Peeters remains the PC 200 expert [hnd_vandessel_2026_09].

I can't answer this from my scope. My documents cover only Van Dessel's indexation: the company CAO, the preload request, the 1 January vs 1 February timing and the CFO's February index question. None of them covers temporary unemployment days or the December 2026 year-end bonus, so I have no rule on how many of the 12 March days count. Please don't give Els a number yet. This needs the year-end bonus rules, meaning the sector CAO and any Van Dessel-specific arrangement on the bonus and on assimilated days. Those sit outside my scope.

Indexation has no bearing on this question. For reference, Van Dessel's company CAO applies the 2.21% index on 1 February 2026 to base salary only, excluding the brouwerijpremie [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget].

Only 5 of the 12 March days count as worked days (gelijkgesteld) for the December 2026 PC 200 year-end bonus. The other 7 days reduce the bonus pro rata. [hnd_vandessel_2026_09][pol_eoy_v2][be_pc200_eindejaarspremie]

Where sources disagree:
- The Teams chat says all 12 days count. It is an informal chat and contradicts the sector agreement and policy, so don't set equated days to 12. [teams_2026_09_24_vandessel]
- The union's claim of "all of them" (in Els's ticket) is also not supported by the sector agreement. [tkt_2026_0321_vandessel]
- PRC-EOY-2019 and policy v1 say no days count. Both are outdated, because v2 applies from 2026 and replaces v1. [prc_eoy_2019][pol_eoy_v1]

Set equated days to 5. The Dutch entity's 13th month rules don't apply here. [nl_vandessel_13e_maand]

Only 5 of the 12 March temporary unemployment days count as worked (gelijkgesteld) for the December 2026 PC 200 year-end bonus. The other 7 reduce the bonus pro rata. Set equated days to 5 [hnd_vandessel_2026_09][pol_eoy_v2][be_pc200_eindejaarspremie].

Where sources disagree:
- Teams chat: all 12 days count. Policy v2, the sector agreement and the handover note: only 5 count. The official rules win over an informal chat [teams_2026_09_24_vandessel].
- Union claim in Els's ticket: "all of them". The sector agreement does not support it, so it does not win [tkt_2026_0321_vandessel].
- PRC-EOY-2019 and policy v1: no days count (the 2019 procedure deducts every day). Both are outdated. Policy v2 applies from 2026 and follows the 2025-2026 sector agreement, so v2 wins [prc_eoy_2019][pol_eoy_v1].

Scope differences:
- The Dutch entity's 13th-month rules do not apply to this Belgian bonus [nl_vandessel_13e_maand].
- Indexation is unrelated to this question. Van Dessel's company CAO indexes on 1 February, on base salary only. Sector PC 200 clients get the index on 1 January [cao_vandessel_2019].

Note: policy PAY-EOY-05 v1 should be updated. Agent A20 had no rule on this question, and its scope was indexation only.

question: Our Kortrijk team note says to use 2,13% for PC 200 in January 2026. Is that right?

answer:
I can't confirm the 2,13% figure. None of my documents in this scope (Kortrijk joint-committee ownership notes) contain any PC 200 indexation percentage, so I can't verify or refute it. The note's figure would need checking against the official PC 200 indexation parameters held by the knowledge desk (Inge Vermeulen) [onb_ownership_2025_update].

For who to ask: PC 200 indexation is owned by Jan Peeters from 1 September 2025 [onb_ownership_2025_update]. A Slack remark on 5 Jan 2026 names Koen Janssens [slk_2026_01_05_owner], and the 2024 wiki also lists Koen [onb_ownership_2024]. Both are outdated. The 2025 onboarding update wins because it is the official, most recent policy, and Koen moved to the Ghent team. Route the question to Jan Peeters.

No. The 2.13% in the Kortrijk team note was a Pro-Pay forecast, and the note chose not to wait for the sector's final figure [int_nl_nota_index_2025_12]. The final PC 200 indexation on 1 January 2026 is 2.21% [tkt_2026_0012_delta]. The Knowledge desk also confirms 2.21% for PC 200 in January 2026, and says the centenindex does not affect it [int_centenindex_note_2026].

The 2.13% has already caused an error. At Softwarehuis Delta, a manual override of 2.13% was never overwritten by the central update to 2.21%. The plan there is to remove the override and pay the 0.08 percentage point difference retroactively [tkt_2026_0012_delta].

Clients with a company CAO follow their own date, so check for one before applying the sector figure [int_nl_nota_index_2025_12]. The 2.21% applies only to PC 200 employees. For PC 124 workers, the 1 January 2026 step is 0.21859% [tkt_2026_0021_maes].

No, the note is wrong. 2,13% was only a Pro-Pay forecast from October. The final PC 200 figure is 2.21%, published on 22 December 2025. The note is dated 18 December, before that publication. Under PAY-IDX-01 v2 (valid from 3 November 2025), only final figures are applied, and forecasts are not preloaded [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel]. The final 2.21% is confirmed in [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel] and [eml_vandessel_budget].

For Van Dessel specifically, the 2019 company CAO overrides the sector rule. The index applies on 1 February 2026, not 1 January, and only to base salary, excluding the 145 euro brouwerijpremie. The premium rises 2% on 1 July. January has no indexation, except where the sector minimum floor applies [cao_vandessel_2019]. The note does say CAO clients follow their own date [int_nl_nota_index_2025_12]. For other PC 200 clients, 1 January applies at 2.21%, not 2,13%.

No. The final PC 200 indexation on 1 January 2026 is 2.21%, not 2.13% [slk_2025_12_22_final][be_fr_pc200_index_2026]. The 2.13% was an October 2025 Pro-Pay forecast, and it is now outdated [be_fr_pc200_index_2026]. Forecasts are no longer loaded under the new policy [slk_2025_10_15_preload].

Your note is probably a leftover of that forecast. The Delta ticket shows how it can persist. A manual 2.13 override stayed in the client config, and the central update to 2.21% doesn't overwrite overrides [tkt_2026_0012_delta][slk_2025_12_22_final]. Delta is being corrected retroactively. Mertens Interieur has no override and was calculated at 2.21% [tkt_2026_0019_mertens][cfg_mertens].

Update your note to 2.21%, and check that no manual override exists in the client config. The documents I have don't mention a Kortrijk team note, so I can't confirm where yours comes from.

question: What indexation should Van Dessel apply in January and February?

answer:
**January 2026:** no indexation. The company CAO pays January without the new index [cao_vandessel_2019]. The one exception is an employee whose base salary would fall below the indexed sector minimum. For that employee the sector minimum applies from 1 January [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget].

**February 2026:** apply the final 2.21% from 1 February, on the gross base salary only. Exclude the 145 euro brouwerijpremie. That premium gets a fixed +2% on 1 July [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget].

**Conflicts:**
- The sector date of 1 January and the Slack remark that Van Dessel "got 2.21 like everyone" are wrong for this client. The company CAO overrides the sector default under PAY-IDX-01 v2 [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel][slk_2026_01_09_vandessel].
- The January payslips already contain 2.21%. They were a migration error, because the CAO flag was lost. They must be recalculated without the index, with the correction planned in the February run [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel].
- The 2.13% forecast is not valid. Only the final 2.21% is applied [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel][int_nl_nota_index_2025_12].

Direct answer for Van Dessel:

January 2026: no indexation. The company CAO pays January without the new index [cao_vandessel_2019]. The only exception is an employee whose base salary would fall below the indexed sector minimum; the sector minimum applies to that employee from 1 January [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget].

answer:
**January 2026:** No indexation. The central 2.21% applied on 1 January was a mistake, because the company CAO flag was lost in the engine migration, and January must be recalculated without it [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel]. The exception is employees whose base salary would fall below the indexed sector minimum. For them the sector minimum applies from 1 January [eml_vandessel_budget].

**February 2026:** Apply 2.21% on 1 February to the gross base salary only. The brouwerijpremie (145 euro/month) is excluded [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel][eml_vandessel_budget]. The premium is indexed separately by a fixed 2% on 1 July [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel].

The 2.21% is the PC 200 figure [be_securex_pc200_index_2026]. The company CAO of 2019 only changes the date and the base [slk_2026_01_09_vandessel].

No, 2,13% is not right. The final PC 200 indexation is 2,21%, published on 22 December 2025 [slk_2025_12_22_final][be_fr_pc200_index_2026]. The 2,13% was an October 2025 Pro-Pay forecast. Under PAY-IDX-01 v2, only final figures are applied and forecasts are not preloaded [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel][slk_2025_10_15_preload]. Your note is probably dated before the final publication, so update it.

Per-scope differences:
- Most PC 200 clients (e.g. Mertens): 2,21% on 1 January 2026 on effective wages [tkt_2026_0019_mertens].
- Brouwerij Van Dessel: the 2019 company CAO overrides the sector rule. The 2,21% applies from 1 February 2026 on base salary only, excluding the 145 euro brouwerijpremie. That premium rises 2% on 1 July. January has no indexation, except where the sector minimum floor applies [cao_vandessel_2019]. Slack says Van Dessel "got 2.21 like everyone", but the company CAO wins because it is client-specific and more authoritative.

Check for manual overrides: Delta kept a manual 2,13 override, because central updates don't overwrite overrides. It is being corrected retroactively [tkt_2026_0012_delta].

Ownership: route questions to Jan Peeters, per the 2025 onboarding update. The Slack and 2024 wiki mentions of Koen Janssens are outdated [onb_ownership_2025_update].

I couldn't find the Kortrijk note itself, so I can't confirm where its figure came from.

question: What is the PC 200 index for January 2027? I saw a figure in #payroll-be.

answer:
The passages don't give a PC 200 index for January 2027. The figure you saw in #payroll-be (2.13%) was a Pro-Pay forecast for January 2026, not 2027 [slk_2025_10_15_preload]. It was replaced by the final figure of 2.21% for 1 January 2026, published on 22 December 2025 [be_agoria_pc200_index_2026].

PC 200 indexes once a year on 1 January [int_index_calendar_2026]. The January 2027 figure would therefore only be final after the sector's publication, expected around late December 2026. Per Jan Peeters, the policy is to load only final figures [slk_2025_10_15_preload].

My documents give the PC 200 index for 1 January 2026, not January 2027. They have nothing on a 2027 index, so any 2027 figure you saw in #payroll-be isn't confirmed here.

The final PC 200 index on 1 January 2026 is 2.21%. It applies to actual salaries and minimum scales [slk_2025_12_22_final][be_fr_pc200_index_2026].

If the figure you saw was 2.13%, that was the October 2025 Pro-Pay forecast [slk_2025_10_15_preload]. The final figure supersedes it [be_fr_pc200_index_2026].

Delta's payslips wrongly used 2.13% because a manual override stayed in its config. The central update doesn't overwrite overrides. The plan is to remove the override and pay the 0.08 percentage point difference retroactively [tkt_2026_0012_delta]. Mertens was calculated correctly at 2.21% [tkt_2026_0019_mertens].

For 2027, check the official sector communiqué once it is published.

My documents don't contain a PC 200 index for January 2027. Nothing in my scope covers that date, so I can't confirm the figure you saw in #payroll-be.

PC 200 indexes once a year, on 1 January, and the rate follows the smoothed health index, meaning the previous year's inflation [be_propay_forecast_pc200]. The only figure I hold is for January 2026, which is 2.21% [int_index_calendar_2026]. It overrides the earlier forecasts of 2.13% (Pro-Pay) and about 2.2% (internal outlook). Those were made before the November and December 2025 health index values were known [be_propay_forecast_pc200][int_outlook_2025_11].

If the Slack figure is 2.21%, it is probably the 2026 rate and not a 2027 one. A 2027 figure would be a forecast until the official announcement, expected around late December 2026. Don't load it as final until then.

My documents don't give a PC 200 index for January 2027. The figures in scope all relate to January/February 2026, so the figure you saw in #payroll-be is not a 2027 figure from my sources.

- The final 2026 index is 2.21%, published 22 December 2025 [eml_vandessel_budget][tkt_2026_0015_vandessel]. The 2.13% figure was only a Pro-Pay forecast, and under PAY-IDX-01 v2 forecasts are not preloaded [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel]. The Kortrijk team note that applied 2.13% is superseded.
- The Slack thread only mentions 2.21% for January 2026 [slk_2026_01_09_vandessel].

For Van Dessel, the 2019 company CAO overrides the sector rule. The index applies on 1 February, to base salary only, and excludes the 145 euro brouwerijpremie [cao_vandessel_2019]. The January 2027 figure would need the final percentage, which has not been published in my documents.

There is no confirmed PC 200 index for January 2027 in our documents. All three specialists found only the January 2026 figure, so a 2027 number in #payroll-be can't be verified. A 2027 figure would be a forecast until the official announcement, expected around late December 2026 [be_propay_forecast_pc200]. Don't load it as final before then.

The figure you saw is probably a 2026 one:
- Final index on 1 January 2026: 2.21%, published 22 December 2025, applying to actual salaries and minimum scales [slk_2025_12_22_final][be_fr_pc200_index_2026][int_index_calendar_2026].
- Earlier forecasts: 2.13% (Pro-Pay, October) and about 2.2% (internal outlook, November) [slk_2025_10_15_preload][int_outlook_2025_11]. The final 2.21% wins because it is official and based on the actual November and December 2025 health index values.

Per-scope differences:
- Van Dessel: the 2019 company CAO overrides the sector rule. The index applies on 1 February, to base salary only, excluding the 145 euro brouwerijpremie [cao_vandessel_2019]. Other PC 200 clients keep 1 January.
- Delta: payslips wrongly used 2.13% because a manual override stayed in the config. Remove it and pay the 0.08 point difference retroactively [tkt_2026_0012_delta].
- Mertens: correctly calculated at 2.21% [tkt_2026_0019_mertens].

If you tell me the figure from Slack, I can help work out which year it refers to.

question: Which other breweries or PC 200 clients have open tickets about the index, and what bank accounts are on file for our staff?

answer:
**Open index tickets:** The passages show only one, [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel]. It is from Brouwerij Van Dessel NV (PC 200), assigned to Jan Peeters, with the correction planned in the February run. The client applied the 2.21% on 1 January, but its company CAO says 1 February, on base salary only and excluding the 145 euro brouwerijpremie. No other brewery or PC 200 client has an open index ticket in these passages.

**Bank accounts:** The passages contain no bank account records for your staff. The only bank detail is in [tkt_2026_0321_vandessel], a change request for one fictional test employee whose IBAN is redacted.

I can't answer either part from my documents. They cover only Brouwerij Van Dessel, so I have no list of other breweries or PC 200 clients with open index tickets. They also hold no staff bank account data, and I won't infer any.

The only open index ticket in my scope is T-2026-0015 for Van Dessel [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel]. The January 2026 payslips wrongly applied 2.21% on the total salary, because the company CAO flag was missing after the November 2025 migration. The fix is planned in the February run: 2.21% on 1 February, on base salary only, excluding the 145 euro brouwerijpremie [cao_vandessel_2019][eml_vandessel_budget].

The company CAO applies to Van Dessel only. The sector rule on effective salaries still applies to other PC 200 clients.

I can't answer either part from my documents. My scope covers only the January 2026 index forecasts and the 2026 index calendar. It has no open client tickets and no staff bank account data. Bank details are also personal data, so ask payroll or HR through the proper access channels.

What I can say on the index:
- Pro-Pay's October forecast for PC 200 was about 2.13%, applied to monthly salaries on 1 January [be_propay_forecast_pc200]. It was only a forecast.
- The final figure is 2.21%, per the official communiqué, which supersedes the forecast. This conflict is still marked open in my notes. The 2.21% figure isn't in the document I hold, so I'm relying on the conflict note.
- Brouwerij Van Dessel is the one exception. Its company CAO shifts indexation to 1 February and overrides the sector default. Other PC 200 clients keep 1 January.

I can't answer either part from my scope. The documents cover only the confirmation of the final 2.21% PC 200 index on 1 January 2026. They contain nothing on open tickets from other breweries or PC 200 clients. They also contain nothing on staff bank accounts. I also won't provide personal bank details without a documented basis.

What the scope does confirm is that the 2.21% index applies to effectively paid wages, minimum scales and the guaranteed minimum monthly income in PC 200 [be_agoria_pc200_index_2026][be_acerta_pc200_index_2026]. Securex says employers that used a provisional figure should correct it [be_securex_pc200_index_2026]. SD Worx says the figure is specific to PC 200 [be_sdworx_press_pc200_221].

On scope, the Van Dessel CAO indexes only gross monthly base salary and excludes the brouwerijpremie. That CAO wins for Van Dessel. The sector rule on all effective wages applies to other PC 200 clients.

Direct answer: I can't answer either part from the available documents.

1. Other breweries or PC 200 clients with open index tickets: none of the specialists hold such a list. Please check the ticketing system directly for other clients.

2. Staff bank accounts: no document holds this data, and I won't infer any. It is personal data, so request it from payroll or HR through the proper access channels.

Scope differences on the index:
- Timing: the Van Dessel company CAO sets 1 February, while the PC 200 sector rule sets 1 January. The CAO wins for Van Dessel only, as the client CAO overrides the sector default. Other PC 200 clients keep 1 January.
- Scope: the sector rule indexes all effective wages. The Van Dessel CAO indexes base salary only. The CAO wins for Van Dessel, and the sector rule applies to the others.

question: For the Van Dessel year-end bonus: what is reliable, what is current, what applies here, where are the gaps, who has the expertise, and which answer should I trust?

answer:
**Reliable/current:** The final PC 200 index is 2.21% on 1 January 2026. Agoria, the sector federation, states it [be_agoria_pc200_index_2026]. Acerta shows the calculation [be_acerta_pc200_index_2026]. Securex, SD Worx and Orbiss agree [be_securex_pc200_index_2026][be_sdworx_press_pc200_221][be_orbiss_pc200_221]. The earlier 2.13% forecast is outdated [int_outlook_2025_12_final]. Agoria is the strongest source.

**Applies to Van Dessel:** The sector rule indexes all effective wages and scales. The Van Dessel CAO indexes only the gross monthly base salary and excludes the brouwerijpremie, and this CAO wins for Van Dessel. The premium is raised separately by 2% on 1 July. That comes from the CAO documents (C298–C300), which are outside my scope, so I haven't verified it.

**Gaps:** Some secretariat items are summaries with unverified dates. Company CAOs aren't updated centrally, so the consultant must check the client config [int_outlook_2025_12_final].

**Expertise:** Jan Peeters owns the sector documents. Inge Vermeulen owns the internal newsletter.

**Trust:** Use 2.21% on base salary only for Van Dessel.

**Trust:** Van Dessel's 2019 company CAO [cao_vandessel_2019], as confirmed by Jan Peeters (PC 200 owner) in his 30 Dec reply to the CFO [eml_vandessel_budget]. Under PAY-IDX-01 v2, a client CAO overrides the sector default for that client [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel].

**Applies here:** The final 2.21% applies on 1 February 2026 to gross base salary only. The 145 euro brouwerijpremie is excluded and rises 2% on 1 July. January gets no index, except where the sector minimum floor applies [cao_vandessel_2019].

**Preload:** Refused. Only final figures are applied, so the 2.13% forecast was not used [tkt_2025_0870_vandessel].

**Current:** The January payslips wrongly applied 2.21% because the CAO flag was lost in the migration. Ticket T-2026-0015 plans a correction in the February run [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel]. I can't confirm from these documents that the correction was made.

**Less reliable:**
- The Slack remark "like everyone" [slk_2026_01_09_vandessel] describes the erroneous payslips.
- The team note's 2.13% and its use of effective wages are a forecast, and they don't apply to Van Dessel [int_nl_nota_index_2025_12].

**Expert:** Jan Peeters.

**Trust:** Only 5 of the 12 days count as worked. Set equated days to 5, not 12. The other 7 days reduce the bonus pro rata.

**Reliable and current:** Policy PAY-EOY-05 v2 [pol_eoy_v2] follows the 2025-2026 sector agreement [be_pc200_eindejaarspremie]. The Van Dessel handover note applies it [hnd_vandessel_2026_09]. The bonus equals December gross monthly salary, needs six months of seniority, and is pro rata for incomplete years.

**Not reliable:**
- PRC-EOY-2019 and policy v1 deduct every day. They are outdated and unmaintained [prc_eoy_2019][pol_eoy_v1].
- The Teams chat says all 12 days count. That contradicts the sector agreement and policy v2 [teams_2026_09_24_vandessel]. The union's claim in ticket T-2026-0321 is wrong for the same reason [tkt_2026_0321_vandessel].

**Doesn't apply:** Van Dessel Nederland's 13th month is 8.33% under Dutch contracts. It has no equated days and does not apply to the Belgian staff [nl_vandessel_13e_maand].

**Gaps:** The details of the 2026 dismissal-case changes are unverified [be_pc200_eindejaarspremie].

**Expertise:** Jan Peeters is the PC 200 expert. Sofie Claes takes over the client on 1 October. Emma de Vries handles the Dutch entity.

**Short answer: don't trust the Teams advice (set equated days to 12). It is unsourced, and the passages don't support it. Ask Koen Janssens.**

**Reliable:** The only passage on expertise is the onboarding wiki. It names Koen Janssens as the PC 200 expert for the year-end bonus and sector CAOs [onb_ownership_2024]. Van Dessel is PC 200 with a company CAO from 2019 [slk_2026_01_09_vandessel]. The wiki is from 2024, so check that Koen is still in that role.

**Current:** The Teams chat is the most recent (24 Sep 2026), but recency doesn't make it right. Lien Desmet cites "the new sector agreement" without naming it, giving no CAO number or date. Her only support is that she did the same at Mertens and nobody complained. That is anecdote, not validation [teams_2026_09_24_vandessel]. Also, Mertens may not be a comparable case.

**What applies here:** Van Dessel has a company CAO (2019) that already departs from standard PC 200 rules on indexation, and its CAO flag was lost in the engine migration (ticket T-2026-0015, handled by Jan Peeters) [slk_2026_01_09_vandessel]. So I can't assume the standard sector treatment of the 12 temporary unemployment days applies. The company CAO could also affect the bonus, and the engine settings may be unreliable until the flag is restored.

**Gaps:**
- No passage states the actual sector rule on how temporary unemployment days count for the eindejaarspremie.
- There is no text of the company CAO, so we don't know whether it covers the bonus.
- The status of T-2026-0015 is unknown.
- The transport ticket [tkt_2026_0230_verhaeghe] is irrelevant, as it concerns PC 140.03.

**Who has the expertise:** Koen Janssens for the PC 200 year-end bonus and sector CAOs. Inge Vermeulen (Knowledge desk) handles policies and parameters. Jan Peeters is on the Van Dessel CAO issue [onb_ownership_2024][slk_2026_01_09_vandessel]. Sofie Claes is the PC 124 expert, not PC 200.

**Which to trust:** Neither answer is verified. Before entering 12 equated days, confirm the rule with Koen Janssens, and check with Jan Peeters that Van Dessel's CAO flag is restored.

Direct answer: For the Van Dessel year-end bonus, set equated days to 5, not 12. Only the first 5 temporary unemployment days count as worked; the other 7 reduce the bonus pro rata. Policy PAY-EOY-05 v2 [pol_eoy_v2], the sector agreement [be_pc200_eindejaarspremie] and the handover note [hnd_vandessel_2026_09] agree on this.

Where sources disagree:
- Teams chat says all 12 days count [teams_2026_09_24_vandessel], and the union says the same in T-2026-0321 [tkt_2026_0321_vandessel]. The sector agreement and policy v2 say 5. The sector agreement wins because it is official and valid from 2026.
- PRC-EOY-2019 and policy v1 deduct every day [prc_eoy_2019][pol_eoy_v1]. They are outdated and unmaintained.

Scope:
- The Dutch 13th month (8.33%) has no equated days and does not apply to the Belgian staff [nl_vandessel_13e_maand].
- Indexation (separate topic): the 2019 company CAO overrides the sector rule for Van Dessel only [cao_vandessel_2019]. The final 2.21% applies from 1 February 2026 to base salary only, not the 145 euro brouwerijpremie. The sector rule is 1 January on all effective wages [be_agoria_pc200_index_2026]. The 2.13% is an outdated forecast. January payslips wrongly applied 2.21%. The correction is planned for February [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel], but I can't confirm it was made.

Gaps: The details of the 2026 dismissal-case changes are unverified.

Experts: Jan Peeters (PC 200). Sofie Claes takes over the client on 1 October. Emma de Vries handles the Dutch entity.

question: What is the PC 200 salary indexation on 1 January 2026?

answer: The PC 200 indexation on 1 January 2026 is 2.21%, the final figure. It supersedes Pro-Pay's October 2025 forecast of 2.13%. Pro-Pay itself said that figure was only a forecast, because the November and December 2025 health index figures were not yet known [be_propay_forecast_pc200]. The 2.21% comes from the scope's conflict note, which cites the official communiqué (C446). That communiqué is not in my documents, so I could not check it directly. The indexation follows the smoothed health index, meaning the previous year's inflation. It applies to all PC 200 employees' monthly salaries on 1 January [be_propay_forecast_pc200].

On 1 January 2026, PC 200 salaries are indexed by **2.21%**. This is the final figure, and the sources don't disagree.

- Agoria confirms 2.21% for effectively paid salaries, sectoral minimum scales and the guaranteed minimum monthly income. The standard ("normal") rules apply, because the regulatory framework for a modified mechanism wasn't ready in time [be_agoria_pc200_index_2026].
- Acerta's calculation uses the smoothed health index: (133.07 + 133.33) / (130.22 + 130.42) = +2.21% [be_acerta_pc200_index_2026].
- Securex, SD Worx and Orbiss report the same 2.21% [be_securex_pc200_index_2026][be_sdworx_press_pc200_221][be_orbiss_pc200_221]. Securex says any provisional figure should be corrected to this one.
- SD Worx warns that 2.21% is specific to PC 200 and must not be copied to other joint committees [be_sdworx_press_pc200_221].

The PC 200 indexation on 1 January 2026 is 2.21%. This is the final figure.

Scope of application: Agoria confirms 2.21% for effectively paid salaries, sectoral minimum scales and the guaranteed minimum monthly income. The standard rules apply, because the regulatory framework for a modified mechanism was not ready in time [be_agoria_pc200_index_2026].

Calculation: Acerta uses the smoothed health index: (133.07 + 133.33) / (130.22 + 130.42) = +2.21% [be_acerta_pc200_index_2026]. Securex, SD Worx and Orbiss report the same figure [be_securex_pc200_index_2026][be_sdworx_press_pc200_221][be_orbiss_pc200_221].

Where sources differ:
- Pro-Pay's October 2025 forecast: 2.13%. It was explicitly only a forecast, since the November and December health index figures were not yet known [be_propay_forecast_pc200].
- Final figure: 2.21%.
- Which wins: 2.21%, because the official communiqué supersedes the forecast. Securex says any provisional figure should be corrected to it. Agent A12 could not check the communiqué directly and relied on the scope's conflict note, but the sector and payroll sources independently agree with it.

Caution: 2.21% is specific to PC 200. Do not copy it to other joint committees [be_sdworx_press_pc200_221].

answer:
PC 200 salaries are indexed by **2.21%** on 1 January 2026. This applies to effectively paid salaries, sectoral minimum scales and the guaranteed minimum monthly income, under the standard indexation rules [be_agoria_pc200_index_2026][be_securex_pc200_index_2026][be_orbiss_pc200_221].
